thread.title_full: Fitchburg man pleads guilty to multi-state SNAP and unemployment fraud scheme

author: Bay State News
title: Fitchburg man pleads guilty to multi-state SNAP and unemployment fraud scheme
text:
A Fitchburg, Massachusetts man pleaded guilty on Mar. 24 in federal court in Worcester to participating in a fraud operation that used stolen identities from more than 100 people to obtain $440,000 in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits from Massachusetts and Rhode Island, as well as over $700,000 in Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA) benefits from several states.
The case highlights the scope of identity theft and public benefit fraud during the pandemic period, affecting assistance programs across multiple states. The defendant’s actions exploited vulnerabilities intended to help those facing hardship.
Raul Fernandez Vicioso, age 37, admitted guilt to charges including conspiracy to commit SNAP fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud, SNAP benefit fraud, aiding and abetting, and money laundering. U.S. District Court Judge Margaret R. Guzman scheduled sentencing for July 9. Three alleged co-conspirators—Joel Vicioso Fernandez of Fitchburg; Roman Vequiz Fernandez and Coralba Albarracin Siniva of Leominster—were also charged by criminal complaint.
According to prosecutors, the group purchased stolen personal information from individuals across several states and used it to create fake households for fraudulent SNAP applications listing two Providence apartments as addresses. The defendants also submitted counterfeit documents allegedly photographed at El Primo Restaurant in Leominster—a business operated by Raul Fernandez Vicioso—and used fraudulent benefit cards there for food purchases later sold at full profit through the restaurant.
Investigators said that between April 2020 and December 2021 they obtained over $700,000 by submitting false PUA claims using real victims’ identities with El Primo Restaurant listed as their address. Bank records show more than $276,000 deposited into accounts linked with the restaurant or conspirators; other funds were issued via prepaid cards using known contact details associated with those involved.
During searches of Raul Fernandez Vicioso’s home and restaurant authorities recovered EBT cards obtained through fraud along with documents listing over one hundred identities connected with the scheme. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley announced the plea along with officials from several federal agencies who contributed to the investigation.
The charges carry potential sentences ranging up to twenty years in prison depending on offense type plus fines up to $500,000 or twice the amount involved for money laundering convictions. Prosecutors note that remaining defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.
